note: RFC 4180 reading by a private scanner primitive; the rows-to-JSON mapping is FL over the shared json words. Parameters as CyberChef: cell delimiter (default ","), row delimiter (default \r\n) and format (array of dictionaries, the default, or array of arrays). Each delimiter is a set of characters, any one of which ends a cell or a row, so the default row delimiter reads CRLF, LF and CR; both are read for the escapes \r \n \t \\ and \xHH so they can be typed in a text box. Every value is a JSON string. A cell that starts with a double quote runs to the closing quote and may hold delimiters and line breaks, a doubled quote is one quote, and a quote inside an unquoted cell is kept. Deliberate strictness, each an error rather than a silent repair: an unterminated quote or text after a closing quote is E_COERCE with the offset, line and column; in the dictionaries format a row whose cell count differs from the header, or a repeated header name, is E_COERCE (nothing is dropped or overwritten); the delimiters must be non-empty, must not be the double quote and must not share a character (E_RANGE). Empty lines are skipped. An added indent parameter (default 4 spaces, as CyberChef's JSON output; 0 for compact text) saves a chain step. A byte order mark at the start is dropped, as CyberChef does. Checked against CyberChef 11.5.0 (WP 5.59c): the source of the operation and Utils.parseCSV read, and the delimiters, defaults and the dictionary and array layouts are CyberChef's. Remaining differences: CyberChef toggles quoting at any double quote, also inside an unquoted cell, and drops a last row that has no row end after its first cell (a last line 'c' is lost when the earlier lines were rows); it fills missing cells with undefined and drops extra cells; Forge keeps RFC 4180 reading and raises the errors above.

JSON text parsed strictly by the shared json:parse and written as RFC 4180 CSV by a private writer primitive. Parameters as CyberChef: cell delimiter (default ",") and row delimiter (default \r\n; the escapes \r \n \t \\ and \xHH are read). The input is an array of objects (a header row of the keys, then a row each), an array of arrays (rows only) or one object (a header and one row); every row, the last one too, is followed by the row delimiter (CyberChef's layout). The header holds the keys of all the objects in order of first appearance, with an empty cell where an object has no key (CyberChef takes the keys of the first object only and writes undefined for a key an object lacks). Strings are written as they are, null as an empty cell (CyberChef writes the word null), and numbers, true, false, arrays and objects as their JSON text (big integers exact; CyberChef flattens nested values to a.b keys instead). A cell is quoted when it holds the cell delimiter, the row delimiter, a double quote, a CR or an LF, and a row of one empty cell is written "" so it is not a blank line. Deliberate strictness: an array that mixes objects and arrays or holds other values, a repeated key (JSON text is parsed, so the duplicate is E_COERCE), malformed JSON and a top-level scalar are E_COERCE. Checked against CyberChef 11.5.0 (WP 5.59c): the source read, and the cell quoting rule, the default delimiters and the trailing row delimiter are CyberChef's. An empty array is empty text here and an error there.
